rail_guard.text: Exeter St Davids! For Plymouth, Cornwall, London and everywhere in between. The line along the sea wall at Dawlish is the prettiest in England, when the waves aren't over it.

then.text: Oyez! The city is warned! The bells have rung, the guard is out, and the mayor has put his good hat on.
A rider from Haldon? The beacon's lit? The Armada's in the Channel?
OYEZ! OYEZ! OYEZ! Let it be known that the Spanish are off Plymouth, and every able body is to muster! And to bring a packed lunch!
Exeter's warned. In 1588 the news went on from here, beacon to beacon, all the way to London. Go back and tell Sir Francis. He'll want to know he can stop bowling.

else.text: {greeting} I'm the Town Crier. I shout things, nicely, in a hat. Oyez means 'hear ye', from the old French. Nobody hears me over the buses.
Exeter's been a city since the Romans. They called it Isca. Then came Saxons, Danes, Normans and, worst of all, tourists from Cornwall.

exe_peregrine.text: Look up, on the cathedral. Peregrine falcons nest up there on the stonework. Fastest animal on Earth in a dive.
The pigeons on the Green know it too. You've never seen a pigeon so keen to look busy.

exe_gran.text: {greeting} Cream tea, my lover? Scone, split, clotted cream on first, then jam on top. That's the Devon way. In Cornwall they do it backwards and call it right.
It's not just Exeter that's fussy, mind. The monks at Tavistock Abbey were said to feed their workmen bread with cream and jam a thousand years ago. We've had time to get it right.

exe_grecian.text: Up the Grecians! That's Exeter City. Nobody knows for sure why we're the Grecians. There are four theories and a fifth one my dad made up.
St James' Park is just up the road. Not the London one. Ours has a better view of the allotments.

exe_boatman.text: There's been a little ferry across the Exe here for longer than anyone remembers. Pulled across on a cable, by hand. Very good for the arms.
The wool trade made this quay. Devon cloth, serge mostly, shipped all over Europe. Exeter was one of the richest cities in England on the back of a sheep.

exe_moved.text: That's the House That Moved, across the way. 1961, they put it on rails and inched it along the street. Gran watched it go by with her shopping.
It took days. Not one window broke. You couldn't get a sofa through our front door without breaking three.
